vulnerability_analysis: The Allin contract has a setFees() function that can be called by authorized addresses (owner or authorized accounts). There's no upper bound check on the fees - they can be set to extremely high values (e.g., 5000/10000 = 50%). When users transfer tokens, excessive fees are collected in the contract as BNB. The marketingFeeReceiver (controlled by the attacker) can then drain all accumulated BNB using manualSend().
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner (or become authorized). 2. Enable trading if not already enabled. 3. Set fees to an extremely high value (e.g., 5000/10000 = 50%). 4. Acquire some Allin tokens. 5. Perform token transfers to generate excessive fees. 6. Trigger swapBack() to convert fees to BNB. 7. Call manualSend() to drain BNB to marketingFeeReceiver (which we control).
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the owner. 2. Call tradingStatus(true) to enable trading. 3. Call setFees() with high values (e.g., 5000 total fee). 4. Optionally set marketingFeeReceiver to attacker address. 5. Get some Allin tokens from the initial holder. 6. Transfer tokens between accounts to generate fees. 7. Trigger swapBack if needed. 8. Call manualSend() to drain BNB to attacker.
